inputs_used: content/posts/javanese-wedding-traditions/03-source-pack.json (fact_111 to fact_119 checked for the legal and Smartraveller items)
content-system/personas/*.yaml (weights: planner_couple 0.40, funding_parent 0.20, uhnw 0.20, sceptic 0.10, search_visitor 0.10)

must_fix.issue: Repeated 'It is often told' hedging (8 uses) makes the best-known rites read as unsourced and slows phone skimming. Raised by 3 personas, including the primary.
must_fix.fix: One framing line per section; no new facts and no hedge turned into a bare claim. Keep r2 line 39 ("It is often told that families consult the Javanese calendar and weton, the day of birth, when setting a date, so ask before you hold any dates.") as the only framing line in Before the day. Panggih: keep r2 line 103 ("It is often told that a sindur cloth is draped over the couple as the bride's parents lead them forward (sindur binayang)...") as the framing line and change the end of line 97 ("It is often told that whoever lands first will love more, a folk reading rather than a rule.") to "Folklore says whoever lands first will love more." Attire H2: keep line 131 ("It is often told that Solo brides choose between styles known as Solo Putri and Solo Basahan...") as the framing line; change line 139 ("It is often told that the parents of the couple wear truntum batik, and that the couple themselves wear sido mukti.") to "Custom has the parents in truntum batik and the couple in sido mukti." and line 141 ("It is often told that grooms also wear a beskap jacket and blangkon headcloth for other parts of the day.") to "By custom, grooms also wear a beskap jacket and blangkon headcloth at other points." Gamelan line 155 ("It is often told that pieces such as Kebo Giro accompany the bride's entrance") stays (only one in its section). Net effect: about 12 words saved, which funds the additions below.

must_fix.issue: The criminal code line raises a legal worry with no follow-up, so it alarms rather than informs (trust risk about legality).
must_fix.fix: Replace r2 line "Smartraveller also notes that the revised criminal code includes penalties for cohabitation and sex outside marriage. <!-- fact_117 -->" with "Smartraveller also notes that the revised criminal code includes penalties for cohabitation and sex outside marriage; for unmarried people, authorities can act on a complaint from a child or parent. <!-- fact_117 --> Read Smartraveller's local laws section before you book rooms." Uses fact_117 only. No interpretation of what it means for engaged couples or shared villas; that stays an open question, not article copy.

should_fix.issue: Legal section is a wall of text on a tablet; the parent who will forward it to her partner wants short steps, and the UHNW reader finds it over-long. Section and H2 stay (brief must_include).
should_fix.fix: Turn r2 paragraphs starting "An Australian marrying in Indonesia applies for a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI)..." and "Muslim weddings are performed by the KUA, which issues the marriage book." into 5 short numbered steps, same facts and fact markers: 1. Confirm you share a recognised religion (fact_111, fact_112). 2. Apply for a CNI from the post for your region: Yogyakarta, the Embassy in Jakarta; Solo and East and Central Java, Surabaya; Bali, the Consulate-General in Bali (fact_113). 3. Registries do not normally accept a CNI issued more than 3 months before (fact_113). 4. Muslim weddings: the KUA performs the wedding and issues the marriage book; other faiths: lodge a Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before, then register there afterwards (fact_114). 5. Keep the CNI and the notice inside the same window. Delete "Time the CNI and the notice to fall inside the same window." (now step 5). Trim connective words so the list is shorter than the prose it replaces. Leave the opening disclaimer, the embassy paragraph and the recognition paragraph as prose.

should_fix.issue: The search query is not answered in the first screen: the 12 custom names are buried in sections and the FAQ. Secondary persona, medium severity; also helps the primary persona skim on a phone.
should_fix.fix: Replace the intro sentence "Javanese wedding traditions make most sense in that order, so this guide walks through 12 of them as families tend to hold them." with "Javanese wedding traditions make most sense in that order, so we walk through 12: nontoni, lamaran, peningsetan, pasang tarub, siraman, midodareni, the akad, panggih, sungkeman, paes ageng, batik and gamelan." Names only, matching the existing H3s; keeps the primary keyword in the first 100 words. About +5 words, funded by the hedge cuts.

consider.issue: Older guests: what to have ready if something goes wrong. The paying parent asks this; Smartraveller gives emergency numbers we already hold.
consider.fix: Extend r2 line "Keep a weather and transfer Plan B for outdoor rites." to "Keep a weather and transfer Plan B for outdoor rites, and give older guests Smartraveller's local emergency numbers: ambulance 118, medical emergencies 119. <!-- fact_118 -->" Smartraveller facts only. Nothing on hospitals, insurance or access, which we have not sourced. Apply only if the word count still balances after the items above; otherwise skip.

keep: Intro opener: "A Javanese wedding is not one ceremony. It is a sequence that can begin months before the day..." (praised by all 5)
Framing line "Customs vary by family, faith and region, and where a detail comes from the royal palace in Yogyakarta, we say so."
Key takeaway on siraman and midodareni falling before the vow, so elders arrive early (planner_couple, funding_parent)
Key takeaway on the legal steps for Australians (kept; funding_parent and sceptic trust it)
Siraman: "plan two private bathing spaces and a gap in the run sheet so elders can move between them" (planner_couple, funding_parent, uhnw)
Midodareni: "It is a quiet family evening, not a hen's or buck's night." plus the early-call warning
Lamaran: "expect the date to be agreed here, by the families, rather than by you and a venue"
Pasang tarub 2022 study detail on tents and plastic flowers, and the Girikerto village source with its limits stated (sceptic)
"We have not found an official source that sets out those differences." in the Solo and Yogyakarta comparison
Numbered H3s with name plus plain-English meaning
Quiet, low-pressure Concierge CTA and the 'fee and inclusions agreed in writing' line
conflicts_resolved: Legal takeaway: search_visitor wants it out of Key takeaways; funding_parent and sceptic trust it. The brief's reader explicitly includes marrying legally in Java or Bali, and the primary persona stopped to read because of it. Kept as the one travel or legal takeaway.

Legal section length: uhnw wants it trimmed or tucked away; the brief makes it must_include and the primary persona shares it with their partner. Kept in place under its H2, made shorter and easier to scan as numbered steps rather than moved.
Title 'You Did Not Know?': planner_couple and sceptic call it clickbait-y (low). The title is the person's choice, so it is not an action. Noted under open_questions.

UHNW scale, exclusive use, security and discretion; sceptic commissions and Java vs Bali coverage; funding_parent deposits, accountability, 2am contact and an Advisor call; planner_couple 'what the Advisor handles' and a real wedding: these are business details deferred by instruction and are not must-fix. No Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md, no paperwork help, and no 'from first idea to the last dance'.

Hedging versus sourcing: sceptic asks for sources on the panggih customs, search_visitor wants confidence. We have no new sources, so the fix cuts the repetition but keeps every unsourced detail framed. No hedge becomes an assertion.

checks.check: Weighted scores use persona weights summing to 1.0 across 5 personas run
Gate: weighted enquiry 1.9 < 3.8 and 2 must_fix, so revise. Not stop: trust 3.8, every persona kept reading, the brief is met.
5 items in total (2 must, 2 should, 1 consider), each quoting the exact r2 line
No prices or fees; every added fact traces to fact_113, fact_114, fact_117 or fact_118 (Smartraveller, embassy); no VERIFY needed
No H2 removed or renamed; protect_keywords untouched; primary keyword stays in the intro
Length: hedge cuts (about -12) and legal list (about -15) offset the custom list (+5), the criminal code follow-up (+20) and the optional emergency line (+15); draft stays within 3,200

open_questions.question: The title 'What Are the Javanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?' read as mildly clickbait to 2 of 5 readers (planner_couple, sceptic). Keep it or change it? Your choice; no change made.

Deferred business details readers asked for: fee model and commissions, deposits and supplier accountability, 2am emergency contact, a call with a Wedded Advisor before booking, what the Advisor covers, a real Javanese or Indonesian wedding to show, Java vs Bali coverage, scale and exclusive use, privacy and NDAs. Which, if any, can a later post or the Concierge page carry?
Readers asked what the cohabitation law means in practice for engaged couples and guests sharing villa rooms. We only state Smartraveller's wording; do not add interpretation without a source.
Accessibility and medical cover for older guests (pendopo access, airport transfers, insurance, hospitals near Yogyakarta or Solo) are unsourced. Research for a future refresh if wanted.

assumptions: The brief's word_count range [2400, 3200] is the cap; the lead says r2 is at the cap, so items are written to be net-neutral.
The legal takeaway stays because the brief's reader and goal include legal marriage in Java or Bali; nothing in the brief says otherwise.
'Custom has' and 'By custom' count as framing, not new factual claims, because they keep the detail marked as tradition rather than sourced fact.
The 12-name list uses the draft's own H3 names; the akad is listed as 'the akad' to cover akad nikah or the religious ceremony.
